teaser: A helper and an agent ask what you used, ask nicely for a pause and a refund, stop the payments either way, and publish what each company did.
core_idea: A service in which a helper, with agents doing most of the work under a behaviour policy, asks a company for its record of your usage while doing its own analysis, then sends a friendly request for a suspend mode and a refund, stops the payments either way, and publishes what each company did in an open register, paid at 10% of three months of savings and 20% of what is recovered.

nodes.label: Subscriptions we keep
nodes.summary: Paid for and barely used, kept because of the data in them and because restarting is painful.

nodes.label: Ask what we used
nodes.summary: A polite request for a detailed account of the usage, not a subject access request.

nodes.label: Our own analysis
nodes.summary: Statements, invoices and the account's dashboards, exported into the person's vault while there is still access.

nodes.label: A friendly request
nodes.summary: Maps what was used and its value, says what is good about the product, and asks for a suspend mode and a refund.

nodes.label: Suspend mode
nodes.summary: Keep the data and the settings without paying; several large services already offer a pause.

nodes.label: Stop the bleeding
nodes.summary: Export the data, then pause or cancel; the payments stop whatever the answer to the refund.

nodes.label: The law is a floor
nodes.summary: Unused months are generally not refundable as of right; the UK rules arrive in January 2027 and move the default towards the customer.

nodes.label: The right of access
nodes.summary: The next step if nobody answers, with a one-month deadline, and only ever a genuine request for the person's own data.

nodes.label: The open register
nodes.summary: Contacts, templates and what each company did, under Creative Commons, recorded as dated facts without adjectives.

nodes.label: The helper's fee
nodes.summary: 10% of the savings for three months and 20% of what is recovered, which only pays if agents do most of the work.

nodes.label: Agents under a policy
nodes.summary: The agent reads and drafts; the person signs in, approves and sends from their own address.

nodes.label: Working inside accounts
nodes.summary: How an agent works inside many signed-in sessions without ever holding the passwords.

quotes.text: Whatever the answer to the refund, the payments should stop.
quotes.why: The value lands on day one, whether or not any money comes back.

quotes.text: A dated row that says "asked twice, no reply as at this date" needs no adjective.
quotes.why: It is how the register gives kudos and holds companies to account without characterising anyone.

figures.caption: One subscription, worked by a helper and an agent for the person who pays for it. Two questions run in parallel, ours and theirs; the evidence meets; a friendly letter asks for a pause and a refund; the payments stop either way; and the answer goes into an open register. The right of access is the dashed box: a next step, not the first.

The helper's agent as a behaviour policy: what it could reach once signed in, whether that is in its mandate, the gap, and what actually stands in the way. Green rows need nothing more; the orange row is held by the person pressing the button; the red rows are where a control is still owed. A proposal written before the first run, not a measured deployment.
